dropped.finding: A failed read-back GET is reported as a definitive negative verdict. When the read-back request errors or returns a non-dict body, `after1`/`after2` become the truthy string "<unread>", so the verdict prints "IGNORED (still set)" — indistinguishable from a genuine platform no-op. This is the exact question the probe (and ticket 4b9e's accept/defect branch) hinges on, so a transient read failure can produce a false 'not cleared' answer.
merged_from: The Q1a/Q1b verdict strings ignore the write PUT's own HTTP status (`s1`/`s2`) when classifying CLEARED vs IGNORED, so an outright REJECTED write (e.g. HTTP 400/errors object) is conflated with an accepted-but-silent no-op. The raw status is embedded in the string and the evidence log, but the CLEARED/IGNORED label is derived solely from the read-back value.
dropped.suggested_fix: Distinguish three states in the verdict: read-back not a dict / sentinel => "UNDETERMINED (read-back failed)"; field falsy => "CLEARED"; field still set => "IGNORED (still set)".
